descripcion: At C2 connotation is manipulated deliberately to shift a reader's sympathy across a whole passage without ever stating an opinion directly — choosing a consistent thread of positively or negatively charged words for one side of an account, which does the persuasive work silently.

ejemplos.texto: She explained patiently, staying composed even as the questions grew sharper.
He went on and on, visibly backtracking whenever the details were pressed.
Neither account is technically inaccurate; the sympathy lies entirely in the word choice.

notas: A consistent connotative thread across several sentences shifts sympathy far more powerfully than any single loaded word, precisely because no individual sentence looks biased.
This is a technique to recognise as a reader as much as to use as a writer — noticing the thread is a form of critical reading, not just style analysis.
Mixing sympathetic and unsympathetic words for the same person within one passage undoes the effect and reads as simply inconsistent.

es.en: Spanish journalism uses connotation just as much, so the principle is familiar. The C2 skill is sustaining one chain of loaded words through a whole passage without an explicit evaluative sentence.
es.es: El periodismo español usa la connotación tanto como el inglés, por lo que el principio es familiar. La habilidad C2 consiste en mantener una cadena coherente de palabras cargadas a lo largo de todo un pasaje sin añadir una oración evaluativa explícita.

de.en: German journalism uses connotation just as much (Reform versus Einschnitt), so the principle is familiar. The C2 skill is sustaining one chain of loaded English words through a passage.
de.de: Deutscher Journalismus arbeitet genauso mit Konnotation («Reform» gegenüber «Einschnitt»), daher ist das Prinzip vertraut. Die C2-Fertigkeit besteht darin, eine zusammenhängende Kette wertender englischer Wörter durch einen ganzen Abschnitt zu ziehen, ohne die Meinung ausdrücklich auszusprechen.

it.en: Italian journalism uses connotation just as much, so the principle is familiar. The C2 skill is sustaining one chain of loaded English words through a passage without stating the opinion.
it.it: Il giornalismo italiano usa la connotazione tanto quanto quello inglese, quindi il principio è familiare. La competenza C2 consiste nel mantenere per tutto il passaggio una catena coerente di parole connotate in inglese senza dichiarare esplicitamente l'opinione.

fr.en: French journalism uses connotation just as much, so the principle is familiar. The C2 skill is sustaining one chain of loaded English words through a passage without stating the opinion.
fr.fr: Le journalisme français utilise autant la connotation, donc le principe est familier. La compétence C2 consiste à maintenir tout au long d'un passage une chaîne cohérente de mots chargés en anglais sans énoncer explicitement le jugement.

pt.en: Portuguese journalism uses connotation just as much, so the principle is familiar. The C2 skill is sustaining one chain of loaded English words through a passage without stating the opinion.
pt.pt: O jornalismo em português usa conotação tanto quanto o inglês, então o princípio é familiar. A habilidade C2 consiste em sustentar ao longo de um trecho uma cadeia coerente de palavras carregadas em inglês sem declarar explicitamente a opinião.

errores: Breaking the connotative thread partway through, mixing sympathetic and unsympathetic words for the same subject.
Choosing words so heavily loaded that the bias becomes visible rather than silent.
Failing to notice a consistent thread when reading someone else's account critically.

autochequeo: Is the connotative thread consistent across the whole passage for each subject?
Is any individual word loaded enough to make the bias visible?
Would a reader notice manipulation, or only a feeling of sympathy or its absence?
Have I used the technique for a genuine rhetorical purpose, not by accident?
Could I identify the same technique if I were reading someone else's account?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the connotative thread used to frame a person or event. Check for consistency and flag any word loaded enough to make the bias visible. Do not rewrite the text.
